trip.title: Pacific Coast Road Trip — Seattle to Los Angeles

travelers.notes: first time on the Pacific coast; all under 21 (US drinking age)

vehicle.dropoff: LAX, 2026-08-14 ~21:00 (Friday 9 PM — trip is car-less Saturday morning)
vehicle.notes: MODIFY RESERVATION: original was pickup 5 PM Aug 8 / drop Aug 13 ($663 for 6 days). New: pickup on landing Aug 8, drop LAX morning Aug 15 (8 days, est ~$1,060 — verify actual). Under-25 young-driver surcharge; put all 3 on contract to rotate drivers. UPDATE Aug 10: drop is Friday Aug 14 ~9 PM at LAX (7 days) — Saturday morning is hotel-shuttle only; verify the adjusted total.

return.note: BOOKED. Morning flight — return the car ~7:30 AM and be airside by ~8:00 AM.

budget_usd.notes: Range $4,700 (frugal) – $5,500. Flights line still reflects old estimate — update with actual Aug 15 fare. Rental is an 8-day estimate pending the Hertz modification. Park fees include Mount Rainier $30/vehicle. NOTE Aug 11: route grew to ~1,900 mi (Eureka push + full Hwy 1), so the ~$290 gas line is low — budget closer to $380.

trip_log: ACTUAL Aug 9 (Day 2): did Rainier as planned, but ended the night at the Quality Inn in Kelso, WA (I-5 exit 39) instead of pushing to Seaside/Cannon Beach. Astoria dinner and the coast arrival didn't happen.

REPLAN Aug 10 (Day 3), COMPRESSED: start from Kelso ~7:15 AM, US-30 through Astoria. Day trimmed to the essentials — Astoria Column/Riverwalk (recovering the missed Day 2 stop), Haystack Rock from the sand, Cape Kiwanda lunch, Thor's Well, Heceta Head. Ecola SP cut (duplicate Haystack view, $10 + slow park road); Neahkahnie is a drive-by photo only; Hug Point/Sea Lion Caves/sandboarding stay cut. Bandon ~6:45 PM — relaxed Face Rock sunset.

TRADE Aug 10: sandboarding (Sand Master Park, Florence, 4:45-6:30 PM) is back IN; Bandon is OUT — sleep Coos Bay instead. Night-drive-to-Brookings idea rejected: ~3 hr of dark curvy 101 past everything scenic, breaking the no-night-driving rule, to save ~90 min. Instead: Coos Bay by ~7:40 PM (daylight), depart 7:15 AM, Samuel Boardman by 9:30 with 2 hours in morning light.

CORRECTION + REPLAN Aug 10 (Day 3): the 9 AM constraint is TODAY'S Kelso departure (not tomorrow). Goal restated: minimize Oregon, maximize California's big things. Day 3 is now an Oregon speed-run — Haystack 45 min, Kiwanda pizza, Thor's Well 30 min, Heceta photo — then push to BROOKINGS ~9:45 PM (last ~90 min dark, accepted deliberately). Astoria Column and sandboarding cut. Day 4 from Brookings: Boardman 8-10 AM, Klamath Overlook, Fern Canyon 12:30-2:30, Founders Grove, Garberville ~5:45 — a full, unhurried CA day. ALSO: Hertz drop is now FRIDAY Aug 14 9 PM at LAX — Day 7 ends with the car return (gas before Griffith, leave by 7:50), Day 8 is hotel shuttle only.
ADD Aug 10: Tillamook Creamery is the Day 3 lunch stop (1:00-1:50, free tour + food hall), replacing the Doryland/Cape Kiwanda detour — keeps Brookings at ~9:30 PM instead of 10:30.

MAJOR REPLAN Aug 10 (from the road): goal is now the Mendocino/Fort Bragg region. Day 3 extends past Brookings all the way to EUREKA CA (~11:45 PM-12:30 AM; Crescent City is the bail-out if anyone is fading). Day 4 = Eureka -> Avenue of the Giants/Founders Grove + Rockefeller Forest -> Garberville lunch -> Chandelier Drive-Thru Tree -> LEGGETT HILL Hwy 1 winding hour (daylight only) -> Westport -> Glass Beach -> MacKerricher/Laguna Point -> Point Cabrillo -> Mendocino Headlands sunset -> sleep FORT BRAGG. Day 5 exits east on CA-20 to Willits at a hard 7 AM to make the 3 PM kayak. CUT: Samuel Boardman (passed in the dark), Fern Canyon + Klamath Overlook (both north of Eureka, Aug 11 reservation forfeited - it was free), Garberville night.

REPLAN Aug 11 (Eureka morning): cut the DUPLICATE stops to buy ~3 hr of road time — Rockefeller Forest (repeat of Founders Grove), Shrine tree (repeat of Chandelier), Westport-Union Landing (repeat of every bluff), Point Cabrillo (repeat of Heceta Head yesterday), Russian Gulch; Glass Beach trimmed to 25 min. Night 4 moves from Fort Bragg SOUTH to GUALALA (~6:45 PM, daylight) via the golden-hour Hwy 1 run through Elk/Point Arena/Sea Ranch. Night 5 is now SAN FRANCISCO for sunset (~8:05 PM) — Salinas CANCELLED. Kayak is the open branch: if still booked, SF midday + Moss Landing 3 PM + return north for sunset; if not, full SF afternoon. Knock-on: Thursday's Big Sur day starts ~2 hr further north, so 6 AM alarm for Point Lobos by 8:45.

FINAL Aug 11 plan (Option B): Eureka 9:30 gas -> Avenue of the Giants/Founders Grove -> Garberville lunch+fuel -> Chandelier Drive-Thru Tree -> LEGGETT HILL -> MacKerricher/Laguna Point seals -> Glass Beach -> CA-20 east to Willits -> US-101 -> MARIN HEADLANDS/HAWK HILL for sunset ~8:05 -> sleep SAN FRANCISCO. Mendocino Headlands and the whole Sonoma coast traded away for SF tonight. Downstream FIX: Wed = SF morning (Lands End/Sutro Baths, walk the bridge, Mission lunch) -> Moss Landing kayak 3-5 -> sleep SALINAS restored (no Bay Area premium); Thu Big Sur back to a normal 6:45 start. Gualala and Fort Bragg nights cancelled.

REVISED Aug 11: dropped the CA-20/Willits inland shortcut and took HWY 1 THE ENTIRE WAY to SF. Willits is a junction town with nothing in it, and the inland route only saved time that would have been spent waiting at Hawk Hill for sunset — real cost of the coast is 30-60 min of hotel arrival. Mendocino Headlands restored (20 min). Golden hour runs Elk/Point Arena/Gualala 5:00-6:15, the wild Sea Ranch-Stewarts Point-Jenner cliff section 6:15-7:45, SUNSET AT BODEGA BAY ~8:05, then inland via Valley Ford/Petaluma (easy highway, no cliffs in the dark) to SF ~9:45. Golden Gate is not lost — they walk the bridge Wed 11:15 AM. ⚠ Fuel in Fort Bragg before heading south.

Aug 11 evening + Aug 12 request: SF night = drive the Golden Gate ~9:40, GHIRARDELLI SQUARE first (⚠ closes ~10 PM weekdays - call ahead), Chinatown walk-through (shops shut, lanterns lit), hotel. Wed reordered for geography (user's order zigzagged SF->Palo Alto->SF->Cupertino): GOLDEN GATE SUNRISE 6:20 at Torpedo Wharf -> PIER 39 sea lions 7:15 (shops shut till 10, sea lions are 24/7) -> STANFORD 9:00 -> APPLE PARK VISITOR CENTER 10:15 (⚠ campus NOT tourable). ⚠ HARD CONFLICT surfaced: 3 PM kayak and starting Big Sur the same day are mutually exclusive. BRANCH A (recommended) = Santa Cruz Boardwalk filler 12:30-2:15, kayak 3-5, sleep Salinas, Big Sur Thu. BRANCH B = drop/cancel kayak, Point Lobos 12:45, Big Sur this afternoon, Pismo ~8:30, Thursday freed.

HARD CONSTRAINT Aug 11 evening: must be in LA before 2 AM Thursday. This FORCES Branch B - the Elkhorn Slough kayak is CANCELLED (it and Big Sur cannot coexist Wednesday). Wed becomes: SF sunrise 6:20 -> Pier 39 -> Stanford -> Apple Park -> BIG SUR compressed (Point Lobos 12:30, Bixby 2:00, McWay 3:45, elephant seals 5:20; PFEIFFER BEACH CUT) -> Morro Bay dinner+fuel 6:50 -> US-101 freeway -> LA ~11 PM, three hours inside the deadline. Thursday is now a FREE LA DAY (Getty Center recommended). Salinas and Pismo nights CANCELLED - book ONE LAX-area hotel with an airport shuttle for Wed/Thu/Fri.

Aug 12 retimed to a 9 AM start (sunrise dropped, ~3 hr more sleep). Pier 39 9:00, Stanford 10:35, Apple Park 11:35, Point Lobos 1:55, Bixby 3:00, McWay 4:30, elephant seals 6:05, Morro Bay 7:30 out by 8:15, LA ~11:45 PM. All Big Sur stops still land in daylight (sunset ~8 PM) and there is ~2 hr of margin on the 2 AM deadline, but the slack is thinner - Bay Area traffic is the risk. Escape hatch: cut Stanford, it saves ~1 hr with the detour.

LA TWO-DAY PLAN (Thu Aug 13 from noon + Fri Aug 14). GRIFFITH MOVED TO THURSDAY so Friday is not a scramble against the 9 PM car return. Thu: In-N-Out at the LAX approach (planes 200 ft overhead) -> THE GETTY 1:15-4:30 (free, closes 5) -> Hollywood/TCL forecourt 5:15 -> GRIFFITH 6:45, sunset 7:45, stay till the city lights -> Los Feliz/Thai Town dinner. Fri: surf Surfrider 10-12 -> Malibu Seafood -> El Matador 1:15 -> Point Dume 2:30 -> SANTA MONICA SWIM 3:45 -> Venice + the canals 5:30 -> GAS + drop bags 7:00 -> HERTZ LAX 8:45 (due 9) -> Uber -> DIN TAI FUNG 10 PM. ⚠ TWO RISKS FLAGGED: DTF at 10 PM may be past last seating (most locations close 9:30-10) and many are walk-in only - call today; and the surf lesson still needs confirming.

TATTOOS added to Friday Aug 14, 4:45-7:30 PM. ⚠ HARD ORDERING CONSTRAINT SURFACED: fresh tattoos cannot go in ocean/pool water for 2-4 weeks, so they MUST come after the surf lesson and the Santa Monica swim - not before. Santa Monica shortened to 2:30-4:00 and POINT DUME CUT to free the time. Flagged: book the shop today (3 walk-ins on a Friday evening is a gamble), bring government photo ID (CA is 18+), do not get sunburnt where you want ink (artists refuse burnt skin), budget cash + 15-20% tip, Venice shop minimums ~$100-150.

ADDED The Lighthouse Cafe (30 Pier Ave, Hermosa Beach) as Thursday's 9:15 PM dinner + live jazz, replacing the Los Feliz dinner. The La La Land club and a real 1949 West Coast jazz room. Chosen for Thursday because Friday is full (tattoos 4:45-7:30, car back 8:45, DTF 10) and because Hermosa is ~10 min from the LAX hotel, so the night ends next to bed. ⚠ FLAGGED: evening shows at LA venues are often 21+ and all three travellers are under 21 — must call about the age policy and cover. Fallback: eat on Hermosa Pier, or the original Los Feliz/Thai Town option.

SWAP Aug 13: swimming and Beverly Hills move to THURSDAY; Getty pushed to Friday. Two structural pins explained: GRIFFITH MUST BE THURSDAY (sunset 7:45; Friday at that hour is tattoos + car return) and ALL WATER MUST PRECEDE TATTOOS. Thu: Santa Monica swim 2:00-3:30 -> Beverly Hills/Rodeo 4:15-5:30 (city garages = 2 hr FREE) -> Chinese Theatre 5:50 only if clear by 5:35 -> GRIFFITH 6:45 -> Lighthouse Cafe 9:15. Fri: surf 10-12 (LAST WATER) -> Malibu Seafood -> EITHER El Matador OR the Getty, not both -> tattoos 5:00-7:30 -> gas 7:45 -> car 8:45 -> DTF 10. ⚠ The Getty is the casualty of the swap: it wants 3 hr, closes at 5, and Friday only offers a rushed 2:45-4:30 before the tattoo appointment.

⚠ NEW RISK Aug 13: Friday night is a DIFFERENT hotel and its location is unknown. Consequences: check out of hotel #1 Friday morning with all bags riding in the car all day; check into hotel #2 ~7:45 PM just before the 9 PM car return; and from 9 PM they are CAR-LESS, so hotel #2 must be Uber-reachable to Din Tai Fung and — critically — to LAX on Saturday for the 10:59 flight. If no airport shuttle, Uber ~8:15 AM, budget $40-60.

FINAL two-day LA plan (Aug 13-14). SURF LESSON CANCELLED (never booked) — frees Friday morning and means El Matador AND the Getty both fit; also makes Thursday's Santa Monica swim the ONLY ocean of the trip. NO ROOM BOOKED for Thursday night and bags have been in the car since the Hilton noon checkout — book LAX/El Segundo/Hawthorne immediately AND FOR BOTH NIGHTS, cancelling Friday's unknown hotel if refundable. That one change removes the Friday checkout, the all-day bags-in-car exposure, the 7:45 PM check-in squeeze and the Saturday airport unknown. Check in at 4:15 BEFORE Griffith so luggage is not sitting in a dark Griffith lot 6:45-8:30. Thu: swim 2:00-3:30, check in 4:15, Beverly Hills 5:15-6:15, Griffith 6:45 (sunset 7:45), Lighthouse 9:15. Chinese Theatre cut. Fri: El Matador 10:45, Malibu Seafood 12:00, GETTY 1:30-4:30 full three hours, tattoos 5:00-7:30, gas 7:50, Hertz 8:45, DTF 10:00, Uber back ~11:30. Sat: shuttle/Uber 8:15, airside 9:30, DL2568 10:59.

Aug 13: 2 AM curfew available BOTH nights. In-N-Out slotted 4:35-5:05 Thursday (LAX approach location, 5 min from hotel, best in daylight; open till ~1 AM as a fallback). Three late options added for tonight, ranked by effort: Manhattan Beach Pier (5 min), Santa Monica Pier at night (30 min), Hollywood Blvd at midnight (45 min each way). ⚠ NOTE the 2 AM freedom is far less useful FRIDAY — the car goes back at 9 PM and they are car-less after, so Friday's extra time was spent on daylight instead (Venice canals added after the tattoos).

Aug 13 FINAL: THE GETTY MOVED TO THURSDAY MORNING (~12:15-2:45). Knock-on is all upside — Friday gets ~4 hr back (Getty + the never-booked surf lesson), so POINT DUME and VENICE/the canals both return and the TATTOO SLOT MOVES EARLIER to 4:00-6:30, giving real buffer before the 9 PM car return instead of a sprint. Thu: Getty 12:15-2:45 -> Santa Monica swim 3:05-4:15 (ONLY ocean of the trip) -> check in 4:35 -> Beverly Hills 5:30-6:15 -> GRIFFITH 6:45 (sunset 7:45) -> Lighthouse 9:15-11:00 -> In-N-Out ~11:20 (open till ~1 AM, 5 min from hotel) -> optional Manhattan Beach Pier. Fri: El Matador 11:00 -> Malibu Seafood 12:15 -> Point Dume 1:15 -> Venice + canals 2:45 -> TATTOOS 4:00-6:30 -> gas/freshen 7:00-8:15 -> Hertz 8:45 -> DTF 10:00.

Aug 13 CHANGE: check-in moves to LATE (~midnight, after In-N-Out) rather than 4:35 PM, with Friday-morning checkout. Frees ~40 min, which went to the Santa Monica swim (now 3:05-4:30, 85 min) since it is the only ocean of the trip. ⚠ TRADE-OFF ACCEPTED: luggage rides in the car all day Thursday AND all day Friday. Mitigations recorded: valuables on person, bags into the trunk BEFORE arriving at each stop (never rearrange in the lot - thieves watch for it), attended/paid garages only (Getty garage, Santa Monica pier deck, Beverly Hills city garage), and Griffith 6:45-8:30 is the highest-risk stop of the two days. Also: call the hotel today to hold a ~midnight arrival - small properties release late no-shows.

FINAL Aug 13-14: rooms confirmed BOTH nights (no airport sleeping), NO haircut. Thu: Getty 12:15-2:45, Santa Monica swim 3:05-4:30 (only ocean of the trip), Beverly Hills 5:30-6:15, GRIFFITH 6:45 sunset 7:45, Lighthouse 9:15-11:00, In-N-Out ~11:20, check in ~midnight. Fri: El Matador 11:00, Malibu Seafood 12:15, Point Dume 1:15, Venice+canals 2:45, TATTOOS 4:00-6:30, hotel+gas 7:00-8:15, HERTZ 8:45 (due 9), DTF 10:00, back ~11:30. Sat: shuttle/Uber 8:15, airside 9:30, DL2568 10:59. Remaining actions: tattoo booking, DTF 10 PM seating, Lighthouse 21+ policy, Saturday shuttle time.

Aug 13: In-N-Out moved to right after the Santa Monica swim, at the WESTWOOD branch (922 Gayley Ave) rather than the LAX plane-spotting one. Westwood sits directly between Santa Monica and Beverly Hills (~10 min each way) so it costs nothing; the LAX branch would have added ~30 min of round trip and halved the Beverly Hills hour, putting Griffith parking at risk. Order holds: swim 3:05-4:30, In-N-Out 4:45-5:15, Beverly Hills 5:30-6:15, Griffith 6:45.

Aug 13 FINAL CHANGE: Lighthouse Cafe confirmed 21+ and is CANCELLED — which frees the 9-11 PM block and lets the TATTOOS happen TONIGHT. Thu now: Getty 12:15-2:45, swim 3:05-4:30, In-N-Out Westwood 4:45, Beverly Hills 5:30-6:15, GRIFFITH 6:45-8:30, dinner Los Feliz/Thai Town 8:45-9:45 (EAT BEFORE INKING - low blood sugar in the chair), TATTOOS 10 PM-12:30 AM Hollywood/Sunset, check in ~1:15 AM. Upside: they sleep in a hotel bed for the first night of healing, and Friday 4:00-6:30 is now free. Downside: Friday's El Matador becomes NO WATER AT ALL and the ink must stay out of the sun. ⚠ Must call shops immediately for three chairs at ~10 PM, and check for sunburn from today's swim before driving over.

Aug 13: TATTOOS CANCELLED entirely, and the Lighthouse Cafe is 21+ so it is gone too. Two things come back: HOLLYWOOD BLVD returns tonight (10-11 PM, the Chinese Theatre forecourt is open air and night is the better time for it), and WATER IS BACK ON for Friday — El Matador is swimmable again and a bonus beach block lands 4:15-6:15 at Manhattan Beach or Santa Monica Pier. Thu final: Getty 12:15-2:45, swim 3:05-4:30, In-N-Out Westwood 4:45, Beverly Hills 5:30-6:15, GRIFFITH 6:45-8:30, dinner Los Feliz/Thai Town 8:45-9:45, Hollywood Blvd 10-11, In-N-Out LAX ~11:30 for the planes, check in ~12:15 AM. Fri final: El Matador 11:00, Malibu Seafood 12:30, Point Dume 1:30, Venice+canals 2:45, beach 4:15-6:15, hotel+gas 7:00, HERTZ 8:45, DTF 10:00. Only open action left: confirm Din Tai Fung seats at 10 PM. Money back to the group: ~$270 surf + ~$300-450 tattoos.

Aug 13: Friday takes ALL the options — resequenced west-to-east-to-south so nothing backtracks. El Matador 11:00, Malibu Seafood 12:30, Point Dume 1:30, SANTA MONICA PIER 3:00-4:15 (the pier itself this time, not just the swim), VENICE + canals 4:30-5:45, MANHATTAN BEACH 6:00-6:45 (directly on the line home), hotel+gas 7:00-8:15, HERTZ 8:45, DTF 10:00. Three beaches, all swimmable now the tattoos are cancelled.

trip_log.what: Beaches ran long. Replanned the Friday tail against the 9 PM Hertz deadline: hotel bag-drop capped at 20 min with a hard 8:30 departure, gas on Sepulveda in El Segundo (non-skippable, on the line), Hertz at 8:50. Din Tai Fung escalated from 'verify' to 'call now' — Del Amo's Friday last seating is likely before a 10 PM arrival. Saturday pinned: leave hotel 8:15, LAX Terminal 3, airside 9:30, DL2568 at 10:59.

decisions_made: Extended trip to Aug 15 (8 days, 7 nights) — return flight BOOKED: DL2568 LAX 10:59 AM -> SAT 3:59 PM
Added a full Mount Rainier day (Day 2): sleep at the Ashford gate night 1, hike Paradise/Skyline from ~6 AM, drive to the Oregon coast in the evening
Outbound now lands SEA 2:50 PM (not 12:27) — pick up the car immediately and drive downtown; the car-less Link light rail plan is dead
Added a full LA day (Day 7) ending with Griffith at sunset, sleeping near LAX night 7 — no more racing the beach day to a flight
Skipped Olympic Peninsula entirely (too far north, added ~200mi)
Skipped Sunrise side of Rainier (2+ hr from Paradise; doesn't fit with the evening coast drive)
Sleep in Salinas not Monterey (Car Week Aug 7-16 = sold out/$500+)
Sleep Garberville not Eureka (avoids 45min backtrack to Avenue of the Giants)
Sleep Pismo on night 6 (further south = shorter next morning to Malibu)
Skip Hearst Castle tour in favor of free Piedras Blancas elephant seals
User chose: surf lesson + otter kayak + SoCal swimming (declined ATV dunes)
hard_constraints: Mount Rainier: enter the Nisqually gate BEFORE 7 AM on Aug 9 — early entry has historically been exempt from timed-entry windows, but VERIFY 2026 rules on nps.gov and grab a reservation if required. $30/vehicle (or use an America the Beautiful pass). Grove of the Patriarchs remains closed (2021 flood damage).
Monterey Car Week Aug 7-16: do NOT book Monterey/Carmel/Big Sur lodging
Big Sur Hwy 1 open but Rocky Creek Bridge has 24/7 one-way signal control through Aug 31 (<=15min delay) - check Caltrans QuickMap
Fern Canyon RESERVATION FORFEITED (it is north of Eureka; the new plan runs south). $12 CASH now only needed for Pfeiffer Beach on Day 6.
Car back at LAX FRIDAY Aug 14 by 9:00 PM (modified drop). Gas up before Griffith; leave the observatory by 7:50 PM. Saturday is car-less: hotel airport shuttle ~8:30 AM for DL2568 at 10:59 AM.
Be in LA before 2 AM Thursday Aug 13. Achieved by leaving Morro Bay by ~7:35 PM Wednesday; US-101 south is ~3.5 hr of easy freeway. Kayak cancelled to make this work.

Fri Aug 14: Din Tai Fung 10 PM AFTER the 9 PM car return - it is an Uber trip, not a drive. Torrance/Del Amo is closest to LAX (~20 min); Santa Monica (~25 min) is open later Fridays. VERIFY the kitchen is still seating at 10.
Fri Aug 14 ORDER IS FIXED: surf lesson and Santa Monica swim BEFORE tattoos. Fresh ink means no ocean, pool or hot tub for 2-4 weeks - Santa Monica at 2:30 is the last water of the trip.

Friday hotel #2 location UNKNOWN as of Aug 13. Must be identified today: it determines the 7:45 PM check-in/bag-drop, and Saturday's car-less airport run (shuttle if available, otherwise Uber ~8:15 AM for the 10:59 flight).

safety.warning: Sneaker waves on OR/N-CA coast surge 150+ft up beach with no warning; 24+ West Coast deaths since 2012. Cold water causes loss of limb control in seconds. Rules: never turn back on ocean, stay off beach logs, keep well up the sand. Swimming only in SoCal (lifeguarded, ~69F).
safety.mountain: Rainier: start the Skyline Trail early (parking + afternoon heat), carry water + layers (Paradise is 5,400 ft, weather flips fast), stay on trail — snowfields linger into August. Cell service in the park is near zero; download offline maps.
safety.vehicle_theft: San Francisco: smash-and-grab break-ins are constant at Hawk Hill, Battery Spencer, Lands End, Sutro Baths, Baker Beach and Twin Peaks. Leave NOTHING visible in the rental — take passports and electronics with you, put luggage in the room before sightseeing where possible. ⚠ Aug 13-14: the group is checking in late both nights, so luggage is in the car through the Getty, Santa Monica, Beverly Hills, a dark Griffith lot, and all of Friday's Malibu/Venice day. Load the trunk before arriving at each stop, never in the lot.

must_book_ahead: DONE: Ashford night 1, Hertz modification, Rainier entry (Days 1-2 are behind you; night 2 ended up at the Quality Inn, Kelso WA)
Fern Canyon Aug 11 reservation - NO LONGER USED (free, nothing lost). Cancel it if the site lets you.
Elkhorn Slough kayak — CANCEL IT. The LA-by-2AM constraint makes Wednesday a Big Sur + drive day; the kayak cannot coexist with it. Cancel so you are not charged.
Malibu surf lesson — Fri Aug 14, 10 AM. CONFIRM IT IS BOOKED. Leave the LAX hotel by 9:00.
Rooms: ONE LAX-AREA HOTEL WITH AIRPORT SHUTTLE for ALL THREE nights Wed Aug 12 / Thu Aug 13 / Fri Aug 14. Salinas and Pismo CANCELLED. (Friday needs the shuttle regardless - the car goes back 9 PM.)
Din Tai Fung Fri Aug 14, 10 PM — CALL TODAY. Most locations stop seating 9:30-10 PM and many are walk-in only. Torrance (Del Amo) is closest to LAX; Santa Monica is open later on Fridays.
trip.notes_city_pass: LA CityPASS / Go City assessment (Aug 13): NOT worth buying for this itinerary. Griffith, the Getty, Santa Monica Pier, Venice, Beverly Hills, the Chinese Theatre forecourt and every beach are ALREADY FREE. The passes only pay off on paid attractions — Universal Studios, Warner Bros Studio Tour, Madame Tussauds, Aquarium of the Pacific — and with ~1.5 days left, a booked surf lesson and a tattoo appointment, there is no room for a full-day theme park. Verify current pricing at gocity.com / citypass.com if adding a big paid attraction.

stops.name: SEA — Seattle-Tacoma Airport
stops.desc: DL1045 lands 2:50 PM. Go straight to the Hertz counter — with the later landing there's no car-less downtown window anymore. Wheels by ~3:45, downtown by ~4:15.

stops.name: Pike Place Market
stops.desc: Produce stalls wind down after 5, but the market, chowder, Piroshky Piroshky, and the gum wall are still going. Park once (Pike Place garage) — everything downtown is walkable from here.

stops.name: Waterfront + Seattle Great Wheel
stops.desc: Straight downhill from Pike Place on the rebuilt waterfront promenade. 175-ft Ferris wheel out over Elliott Bay, enclosed gondolas, ~12 min, big Sound + skyline views.

stops.name: Space Needle + Chihuly Garden
stops.desc: 5 min drive from the market. Go up the Needle, or (better value) the Chihuly Garden & Glass next door. Only if you're ahead of schedule — Kerry Park at sunset matters more.

stops.name: Kerry Park
stops.desc: THE Seattle postcard: skyline, Elliott Bay, and — on a clear evening — Mount Rainier floating behind the city. You'll be standing on its summit road tomorrow. Free, 5 min from downtown. Sunset ~8:25 PM; leave by 8 to make Ashford at a sane hour.

stops.name: Sleep: Ashford (Rainier gate)
stops.desc: ~2 hr from downtown. Ashford/Elbe motels and cabins sit 6 mi from the Nisqually entrance — BOOK NOW, it's an August Saturday. Campsite alternative: Cougar Rock (inside the park). Grab breakfast food + hike snacks tonight; nothing opens before 7 AM.

stops.name: Nisqually Entrance
stops.desc: In before 7 AM: historically exempt from timed-entry windows (VERIFY 2026 rules on nps.gov), no line, and first light on the mountain. $30/vehicle, card OK. Full tank in Ashford — no gas in the park.

stops.name: Christine Falls
stops.desc: 69-ft falls framed by a stone bridge, steps from the pullout. Classic quick shot on the climb to Paradise.

stops.name: Narada Falls
stops.desc: 168-ft curtain waterfall; short steep path to the base viewpoint for rainbows in the mist.

stops.name: Paradise — Skyline Trail
stops.desc: The best day-hike in Washington: 5.5-mi loop, ~1,450 ft up, to Panorama Point staring straight at the glaciers. August = peak wildflowers + marmots everywhere. Layers + water; snowfields linger — stay on trail. Shorter option: Skyline to Myrtle Falls (1 mi, flat).

stops.name: Reflection Lakes
stops.desc: The mirror shot of Rainier, right off Stevens Canyon Rd, 10 min past Paradise. Calmest water midday-ish; then backtrack out the Nisqually gate. (Grove of the Patriarchs is still closed — don't detour for it.)

stops.name: Slept: Quality Inn, Kelso WA (actual)
stops.desc: Where night 2 actually ended: Quality Inn at Kelso (I-5 exit 39), instead of pushing on to Seaside/Cannon Beach. Smart call — no midnight coast driving. The coast is ~2 hr away via the Lewis & Clark Bridge and US-30 through Astoria; Day 3 replanned to start from here.

stops.name: Astoria Column
stops.desc: Cut by the 9 AM Kelso departure — California is the goal now.

stops.name: Ecola State Park
stops.desc: Cut: same Haystack Rock you saw free from the sand, plus a $10 fee and a slow park road.

stops.name: Cannon Beach — Haystack Rock
stops.desc: ✅ Done. 235-ft monolith from the sand.
stops.parking: S Hemlock St & E Gower Ave, Cannon Beach, OR

stops.name: Neahkahnie Mountain Viewpoint
stops.desc: ✅ Done — the pullout guardrail view IS the whole stop.

stops.name: Tillamook Creamery
stops.desc: 🅿️ Big free lot at 4165 US-101 N. Free self-guided tour, food hall lunch, ice cream. Out by 1:50 — tonight is long.

stops.name: Cape Kiwanda
stops.desc: Cut: 15-min detour off 101 whose lunch slot went to the creamery.

stops.name: Cape Perpetua — Thor's Well
stops.desc: 🅿️ Gravel turnout at the Cook's Chasm bridge, WEST side of 101 — the well is a 5-min path from there; skip the drive up to the visitor center. ⚠ This is the first thing to cut tonight: dropping it puts you in Eureka 30 min earlier.
stops.parking: Cook's Chasm, Yachats, OR

stops.name: Heceta Head Lighthouse
stops.desc: 🅿️ Roadside turnouts on the ocean side of 101 just SOUTH of the Sea Lion Caves building — the postcard angle across the cove. 10 minutes, then go.
stops.parking: Sea Lion Caves, Florence, OR

stops.name: Sea Lion Caves
stops.desc: Cut — no time on a night-push day.

stops.name: Coos Bay — dinner + FULL TANK
stops.desc: Last real dinner stop before the long haul. Fast food or grocery deli, FILL THE TANK, bathroom, swap drivers, coffee. From here it is ~4.5 hr to Eureka in the dark.

stops.name: Brookings — last Oregon fuel
stops.desc: Top off and swap drivers. You pass Samuel Boardman just north of here in full dark — it is gone from the trip, that is the cost of tonight.

stops.name: Crescent City — BAIL-OUT stop
stops.desc: ⚠ THE SAFETY VALVE. If the driver is fighting sleep, stop here instead of pushing on. Motels on US-101/Redwood Hwy. Costs you ~1.5 hr tomorrow morning and nothing else. Taking this is not failure.

stops.name: Sleep: Eureka, CA
stops.desc: ⚠ BOOK NOW AND CALL AHEAD — you are arriving near midnight and most small motels have no night desk. Pick a chain on Broadway/4th St with a 24-HOUR FRONT DESK (Motel 6, Super 8, Quality Inn, Red Lion) and tell them the late ETA. Sleep in tomorrow; the Mendocino day starts at 9.

stops.name: CA-20 / Willits inland shortcut
stops.desc: Dropped. Willits is a 5,000-person junction town — gas, fast food, an arch over Main St. It only saved time you would have spent sitting at Hawk Hill waiting for sunset anyway. Hwy 1 the whole way costs ~30-60 min of hotel arrival and buys 90 miles of the best coast in Northern California.

stops.name: Point Cabrillo · Rockefeller · Shrine tree · Westport · Russian Gulch
stops.desc: All cut as repeats: Point Cabrillo = Heceta Head again; Rockefeller Forest = Founders Grove + a 50-min detour; Shrine tree = Chandelier; Westport = every other bluff; Russian Gulch = another sea cave.

stops.name: GAS — Eureka, before you leave
stops.desc: Fill up on Broadway/US-101 at the south end of town, grab water + snacks. Next cheap gas is Garberville, 2 hr south. Depart 9:40.

stops.name: Avenue of the Giants — Founders Grove
stops.desc: 🅿️ Signed lot on Dyerville Loop Rd. Exit 101 at PEPPERWOOD onto the 31-mile Avenue — the road itself tunnels through 300-ft coast redwoods, which IS the drive-through-redwoods experience. At Founders Grove, a flat half-mile loop: the 346-ft Founders Tree, and the DYERVILLE GIANT — 362 ft, fell in 1991, now lying along the trail with a 30-ft root ball. Walking its length is the only thing that conveys the scale. Free, no gate.
stops.parking: Founders Grove, Dyerville Loop Rd, Weott, CA

stops.name: Garberville — lunch + FILL THE TANK
stops.desc: Eel River Cafe: grilled cheese or veggie omelet for the vegetarians, chicken sandwich or tuna melt for the other two. ⚠ Cheap gas — fill up, Hwy 1 stations are sparse and pricey.

stops.name: Chandelier Drive-Thru Tree, Leggett
stops.desc: A living coast redwood ~276 ft tall and 21 ft thick with a 6x9-ft hole cut through the base in the 1930s — drive the car straight through it. Small private park, gift shop, short grove walk.

stops.name: Leggett Hill — Hwy 1 begins
stops.desc: ★ Highway 1 starts here at US-101 and corkscrews ~25 miles over the coast range: hairpins through redwood and fir, over a summit, then the descent where the Pacific opens up near ROCKPORT — the first ocean view is the moment. Then ~35 miles of open coastal terrace past Westport. 35-45 mph and the best driving of the trip. ⚠ Carsick-prone rider up front.

stops.name: MacKerricher SP — Laguna Point
stops.desc: ★ Free, no kiosk. Short boardwalk over the headland to a HARBOR SEAL HAUL-OUT — usually dozens of seals on the rocks below, close enough to hear. Tide pools at the base, and the old Haul Road runs flat along Ten Mile Beach.
stops.parking: Laguna Point, MacKerricher State Park, Fort Bragg, CA

stops.name: Glass Beach + FUEL, Fort Bragg
stops.desc: 🅿️ Lot at the end of Glass Beach Dr off W Elm St, 5 min from Laguna Point. The town dumped trash off this cove 1906-1967 and the surf tumbled the glass smooth. ⚠ Picked over for decades — expect scattered pieces, not a carpet, and COLLECTING IS ILLEGAL. ⚠⚠ FILL THE TANK IN FORT BRAGG BEFORE HEADING SOUTH — the next 90 miles of Hwy 1 have only a couple of expensive stations.
stops.parking: Glass Beach Dr, Fort Bragg, CA

stops.name: Mendocino Headlands — quick stop
stops.desc: Back in the plan. A village that looks like coastal Maine, wrapped on three sides by free state-park bluff trail with sea arches and blowholes. 20 minutes: park on Main St, walk to the bluff edge, go. Coffee for the road.
stops.parking: Mendocino Headlands State Park, Mendocino, CA

stops.name: Hwy 1 — Elk · Point Arena · Gualala
stops.desc: ★ Not a stop, the drive. Open cliff above the Pacific through Elk (sea stacks straight offshore), Point Arena, and into Gualala with the sun dropping the whole way. Free turnouts constantly — pull over wherever it looks good. THIS is why you skipped the inland shortcut.

stops.name: Sea Ranch → Stewarts Point → Jenner
stops.desc: ★ THE BEST STRETCH. Past the Sea Ranch (famous weathered-timber architecture on open bluff) the road narrows onto true cliff-edge above the surf all the way to Jenner. At JENNER the Russian River meets the ocean — harbor seals haul out on the sandbar at the river mouth, and the overlook just north of town is spectacular in low light.

stops.name: Bodega Bay — SUNSET ~8:05
stops.desc: ★ Sunset over the water. Bodega Head (the headland west of town) is the best free viewpoint; Doran Beach works too. Also the Hitchcock 'Birds' town — the schoolhouse is up the hill in Bodega. After this, cut inland: Valley Ford → Petaluma → US-101 south, all easy rolling highway, no cliffs in the dark.
stops.parking: Bodega Head, Bodega Bay, CA

stops.name: Drive the Golden Gate Bridge
stops.desc: You cross it anyway coming down 101 from Petaluma — the towers are floodlit and the city opens up on the far side. Free (southbound into SF is the toll-free direction; northbound is tolled and billed to Hertz).

stops.name: Ghirardelli Square — chocolate + ice cream
stops.desc: ⚠ TIME-CRITICAL — do this FIRST tonight. The Original Ghirardelli Ice Cream & Chocolate Shop typically closes ~10 PM on weekdays (later Fri/Sat), so you are arriving near last call. CALL AHEAD from the road. Hot fudge sundae is the thing. 🅿️ Use the Ghirardelli Square garage on Beach St or a Wharf garage — do NOT street-park a loaded rental here.
stops.parking: Ghirardelli Square Garage, 900 North Point St

stops.name: Chinatown — Grant Ave + Dragon Gate
stops.desc: Oldest Chinatown in North America. ⚠ At this hour the shops are shut — but Grant Ave's lanterns and the Dragon Gate at Bush St stay lit and it is a genuinely good night walk. A few late restaurants and bakeries stay open. Treat it as atmosphere, not shopping; 20–30 min, then the hotel.

stops.name: Sleep: San Francisco area
stops.desc: ⚠ BOOK FROM THE ROAD NOW — you are arriving late and going straight there. South San Francisco / Daly City / Millbrae is the cheap chain belt with free parking; downtown lots run $50+/night. ⚠ Break-ins are constant in SF — leave NOTHING visible in the car overnight, bring everything in. You walk the Golden Gate tomorrow at 11:15, so you are not missing the bridge.

stops.name: Golden Gate sunrise — DROPPED
stops.desc: Dropped for a 9 AM start and ~3 more hours of sleep after four hard days. You already got the bridge last night at Battery Spencer and driving across. ⚠ STILL CHECK OUT AND PACK THE CAR — you are not coming back to the hotel.
stops.parking: Torpedo Wharf, Crissy Field, San Francisco, CA

stops.name: Pier 39 — sea lions
stops.desc: Sea lions on K-Dock — the actual attraction, and free. Shops open at 10 but do NOT wait for them; you need to be rolling by 9:45. Coffee and breakfast on the Embarcadero. ⚠ FILL THE TANK before leaving the city — today is ~450 miles.

stops.name: Stanford — Main Quad
stops.desc: Main Quad and Memorial Church (the mosaic facade is the shot). Visitor lots off Galvez St, paid on weekdays. Trimmed to 45 min — today is long.
stops.parking: Stanford Oval, Palo Alto, CA

stops.name: Apple Park Visitor Center
stops.desc: ⚠ You CANNOT tour the ring or the campus. You get an AR model on an iPad, a roof terrace with a distant view, a café, and Park-exclusive merch. Opens 10, free parking on site. Grab lunch to go in Cupertino/Sunnyvale after — best South Indian corridor in the country if you want it.
stops.parking: Apple Park Visitor Center, 10600 N Tantau Ave, Cupertino

stops.name: Point Lobos State Reserve
stops.desc: The north gate of Big Sur and the best short walk on it: Cypress Grove and Bird Island loops, China Cove's turquoise water, sea otters and harbor seals below the bluffs. Small lot fills fast but midweek midday is usually OK. ~$10/vehicle.

stops.name: Bixby Creek Bridge
stops.desc: The most photographed bridge on the coast — 714 ft of open-spandrel arch across a gorge. Use the marked turnouts on the north and south sides, not the shoulder. ⚠ Expect the Rocky Creek one-way signal delay nearby (≤15 min); check Caltrans QuickMap this morning.

stops.name: Pfeiffer Beach
stops.time: + CUT — narrow road, $12 cash, no time
stops.desc: Cut for the LA push: it is a 2-mile one-lane road each way plus $12 cash, and it costs ~40 min you need tonight. Purple sand and the keyhole arch are great but they are not worth arriving in LA at 1 AM.

stops.name: McWay Falls — Julia Pfeiffer Burns SP
stops.desc: An 80-ft waterfall dropping straight onto a cove beach — one of only a couple of tidefalls on the California coast. Roadside pullouts just north and south of the park entrance; the overlook trail has been closed, so the view is from the road. Free from the turnouts.

stops.name: Piedras Blancas Elephant Seals
stops.time: 6:05 PM · 25 min · FREE · last daylight stop
stops.desc: Hundreds of northern elephant seals hauled out along a free boardwalk right off Hwy 1 — molting season in August means a lot of them lying around. No fee, no reservation, docents usually on site. Better value than a Hearst Castle tour and it is right on the road.

stops.name: Morro Bay — dinner + FUEL
stops.desc: The 576-ft volcanic plug rising out of the bay. Fish and chips on the Embarcadero, or fast food if you want the time back. ⚠ FILL THE TANK HERE — this is your last easy stop before the 3.5-hr freeway run to LA.

stops.name: Sleep: LA (LAX area) — arrive ~11:45 PM
stops.desc: ⚠ THE BIG CHANGE: you asked to be in LA before 2 AM Thursday, so tonight ends here instead of Salinas. Morro Bay to LA is ~3.5 hr on US-101 through SLO, Santa Barbara and Ventura — a real freeway, easy driving, rotate drivers. Arrive ~11 PM with three hours of margin. ⚠ BOOK ONE LAX-AREA HOTEL WITH AN AIRPORT SHUTTLE FOR ALL THREE NIGHTS (Wed/Thu/Fri) — simpler, cheaper, and Friday needs the shuttle anyway since the car goes back at 9 PM. Salinas and Pismo nights are CANCELLED.

stops.name: ★ THE GETTY CENTER — this morning
stops.desc: ★ MOVED TO TODAY. Free admission — you pay only parking. Park at the bottom, ride the driverless tram up to Richard Meier's travertine complex: Van Gogh's IRISES, the Central Garden, and a terrace holding downtown, the Hollywood Sign and the ocean in one frame. ~2.5 hr here is enough to do it properly. Even if nobody is an art person, the building and the view carry it. ⚠ Bags are still in the car — the Getty garage is attended and about the safest lot you will use today, but still take valuables up with you.
stops.parking: Getty Center, 1200 Getty Center Dr, Los Angeles

stops.name: 🌊 Santa Monica — YOUR ONLY SWIM
stops.desc: 🌊 ⚠ THE LAST OCEAN OF THE TRIP — the surf lesson is cancelled and tomorrow's tattoos close the water for 2-4 weeks. ~69°F, lifeguarded, gentle, 20 min down from the Getty. Now gets 85 minutes — the freed check-in slot went here, since it is the only swim you get. Pier, Route 66 end-of-trail sign, Muscle Beach rings just south. 🅿️ PIER DECK GARAGE, never the street. Rinse and change by 4:50.
stops.parking: Santa Monica Pier Deck lot, 200 Santa Monica Pier

stops.name: 🛏 Check in — late, after In-N-Out
stops.desc: Rooms are sorted for BOTH nights — no airport floor. ⚠ Call ahead and say you are arriving around midnight so the desk holds it; small properties sometimes release late no-shows. ⚠ Because you check in late, a week of luggage rides in the car through the Getty, Santa Monica, Beverly Hills and a DARK GRIFFITH LOT 6:45-8:30: load the trunk BEFORE arriving at each stop (never rearrange bags in the lot — that is the tell thieves watch for) and keep passports, wallets and electronics on you.

stops.name: ★ Beverly Hills — Rodeo Drive
stops.desc: ★ 🅿️ Beverly Hills city garages give the FIRST 2 HOURS FREE — 461 N Bedford or 345 N Beverly, never the meters. Compact walk: Rodeo Drive, then VIA RODEO (the cobblestone street with the steps — the photo), the Beverly Wilshire at the foot, then two blocks north to the BEVERLY HILLS SIGN and lily pond at Beverly Gardens Park. ⚠ LEAVE BY 6:15 SHARP — Griffith parking is the one thing you cannot be late for.
stops.parking: Beverly Hills city garage, 461 N Bedford Dr

stops.name: ★ Griffith Observatory — SUNSET
stops.desc: ★ ⚠ TONIGHT OR NEVER — tomorrow at 7:45 you are in a tattoo chair or driving to the car return. Free entry, free Zeiss telescope after dark on a clear night. Hollywood Sign one way, the whole basin lighting up the other. ⚠ PARKING FILLS BY 7 — arrive 6:45, or park lower on Fern Dell Dr and walk up, or take the DASH Observatory shuttle from Vermont/Sunset. Stay until the city is fully lit, ~8:30.
stops.parking: Griffith Observatory, 2800 E Observatory Rd, Los Angeles

stops.name: Lighthouse Cafe — CANCELLED (21+)
stops.desc: Confirmed 21+. Off the plan. Its slot became a free evening instead.

stops.name: Tattoos — CANCELLED
stops.desc: Cancelled. Two things come back: the evening is free tonight, and WATER IS BACK ON for Friday — no ink means El Matador, Santa Monica and the South Bay beaches are all swimmable again. Also ~$300-450 stays in the group, on top of the ~$270 from the surf lesson.

stops.name: Dinner — Los Feliz or Thai Town
stops.desc: Straight down the hill from Griffith. Los Feliz (Hillhurst/Vermont Ave) has the range for a mixed table; Thai Town on Hollywood Blvd is cheaper, open late, and the easiest vegetarian ordering of the trip — just say no fish sauce, no oyster sauce.

stops.name: ★ Hollywood Blvd at night — RECOVERED
stops.desc: ★ Cut twice already, back now that the evening is free — and night is genuinely the better time for it. The TCL CHINESE THEATRE FORECOURT is open air and always accessible: nearly 200 sets of handprints and footprints pressed in concrete since 1927. The Walk of Fame is lit and lively, parking is finally easy, and it is 20 min from Griffith and dinner. ⚠ Keep wallets and phones in front pockets — the Blvd draws pickpockets late.
stops.parking: Hollywood & Highland garage

stops.name: 🍔 In-N-Out LAX — the plane one
stops.time: ~11:30 PM · on the way to the hotel
stops.desc: 🍔 The famous one, sitting directly under the LAX final approach — and it is literally on your way to the hotel, open until roughly 1 AM. Even if nobody is hungry after dinner, stand in the lot for ten minutes and watch the arrivals come in low over the sign. ⚠ Fewer jets this late than at midday, but they still come. Vegetarians who do want food: GRILLED CHEESE, off the menu board, always available.
stops.parking: In-N-Out Burger, 9149 S Sepulveda Blvd, Los Angeles

stops.name: 🛏 Check in
stops.desc: Rooms sorted for both nights. ⚠ CALL TODAY and say you are arriving after midnight so the desk holds it. ⚠ Luggage has been in the car since noon: load the trunk BEFORE arriving at each stop, never rearrange bags in the lot, and keep passports and electronics on you. Griffith after dark and Hollywood Blvd are the two stops that matter.

stops.name: Surf lesson + tattoos — both cancelled
stops.desc: Surf was never booked and the tattoos are off. Result: Friday is wide open, water is back on everywhere, and roughly $570-720 stays in the group.

stops.name: ★ El Matador State Beach
stops.desc: ★ The most photogenic beach in LA County — steep staircase and dirt path down to a cove of sea stacks, arches and caves, late-morning light angling through them. ⚠ REAL SHOES, the path is steep and sandy. ✅ Swimmable again now the tattoos are off — but this is open coast with NO LIFEGUARD, so nobody goes past their waist.
stops.parking: El Matador State Beach, 32350 Pacific Coast Hwy, Malibu

stops.name: Malibu Seafood — lunch
stops.desc: Walk-up counter with picnic tables straight across PCH from the water. Veggie burger and fries for the vegetarians; fish and chips, shrimp, or a chicken sandwich for the others. Fast, no reservations.

stops.name: ★ Point Dume
stops.desc: ★ Short climb up the headland to a boardwalk viewpoint: sea lions on the rocks below, the whole Santa Monica Bay curving away east, Catalina on a clear day. Also the beach from the end of Planet of the Apes. Free.

stops.name: 🌊 Santa Monica Pier — properly this time
stops.desc: 🌊 Yesterday you swam here and left. Today you get the pier itself: Pacific Park's Ferris wheel, the ROUTE 66 END OF THE TRAIL sign, the carousel, and the original Muscle Beach rings just south on the sand. SWIM SPOT: walk 3-4 blocks NORTH of the pier, toward the towers at the end of Wilshire/California (~34.014,-118.502). Do NOT swim at the pier pilings (rip currents, no-swim zone) and do NOT swim the stretch just SOUTH of the pier — the Pico-Kenter storm drain empties there and it's Santa Monica's dirtiest water. North side is lifeguarded, ~69°F, towers staffed to ~7 PM in August. 🅿️ Pier deck lot; bags are still in the car so nothing visible.
stops.parking: Santa Monica Pier Deck lot, 200 Santa Monica Pier

stops.name: ★ Venice Boardwalk + the CANALS
stops.desc: ★ Ten minutes down from Santa Monica. Skate park right on the sand (worth watching even if nobody skates), Muscle Beach, buskers and the boardwalk circus — then walk two blocks inland to the VENICE CANALS: silent residential water, arched footbridges, and almost nobody finds them. Give the canals 20 of the 75 minutes; they are the better half. 🅿️ PAID LOT on Washington or Venice Blvd, never a side street.
stops.parking: Washington Blvd or Venice Blvd paid lots

stops.name: 🌊 Manhattan Beach — last stop
stops.time: 🌊 6:00–6:45 PM · free · on the way in
stops.desc: 🌊 The quiet one, and it is directly on the line from Venice back to the hotel. Lifeguarded, ~68°F, a short pier with the Roundhouse Aquarium at the end, and a beach path with none of the Venice chaos. LAST SWIM OF THE TRIP — this time as a bonus rather than the only one. Rinse off here; you shower at the hotel at 7.
stops.parking: Manhattan Beach Pier, 1 Manhattan Beach Blvd

stops.name: 🛏 Hotel — BAG DROP ONLY, 20 min
stops.time: ⚠ 8:05–8:25 PM · OUT BY 8:30 NO MATTER WHAT
stops.desc: ⚠ RUNNING LATE — this is a bag drop, not a check-in evening. Everything out of the car and into the room, rinse the salt off if there is time, done. HARD RULE: if you are not pulling out of the lot by 8:30, stop unpacking and leave — the car matters more than the bags. Repacking for the flight happens after dinner, not now.

stops.name: ⛽ GAS — Sepulveda in El Segundo
stops.desc: ⚠ NON-SKIPPABLE — Hertz bills unfilled tanks at roughly triple pump price. Sepulveda Blvd through El Segundo is lined with stations and it is directly on the line from the hotel to the return. Do NOT wait for a station on Century Blvd; the LAX-adjacent pumps are both the most expensive and the most congested. Search: 'gas station Sepulveda Blvd El Segundo'.

stops.name: Return the Hertz car — LAX
stops.desc: ⚠ THE LAST FIXED THING ON THE TRIP, and tonight there is no slack left in front of it. Tank full. Photograph all four corners, the odometer and the fuel gauge, keep the receipt. Then Uber to dinner — car-less from here. IF YOU ARE GOING TO MISS 9: call Hertz from the road (the number is on the rental agreement) rather than just showing up late — a phone call ahead is the difference between a grace period and a late-return charge.
stops.parking: Hertz Car Return, 9000 Airport Blvd, Los Angeles

stops.name: ★ Din Tai Fung — 10:00 PM
stops.desc: ★ Xiao long bao are the point — pork soup dumplings, eighteen folds each, made behind glass. ⚠⚠ CALL RIGHT NOW, FROM THE CAR. Del Amo commonly closes 10 PM on a Friday, which means last seating is nearer 9:30 — a 10:00 arrival by Uber may simply be too late, and they take walk-ins only. Ask one question: 'what is your last seating tonight?' If the answer is before 10, do not chase the Santa Monica branch — it is 25 min the wrong way from the hotel and you would be car-less. Fall back to a late kitchen you can reach: Torrance's Korean BBQ strip along Western Ave runs late on weekends (verify hours by phone, do not just show up). VEGETARIAN: vegan dumplings, veggie buns, green beans, cucumber salad, hot and sour soup.
stops.parking: Din Tai Fung, Del Amo Fashion Center, Torrance

stops.name: Sleep: hotel — LAST NIGHT
stops.desc: ⚠ SATURDAY IS CAR-LESS. Repacking got pushed to tonight-after-dinner, so do it before anyone lies down: everything liquid into one bag, chargers off the walls, nothing left in the bathroom. ASK THE FRONT DESK ON THE WAY IN whether they run an LAX shuttle and what time the first ones go — if there is one, book 8:15 AM; if there is not, pre-schedule an Uber tonight (budget $25-40 for a hotel this close in, more if it surges). DL2568 is at 10:59 — airside by 9:30.

stops.name: LAX Terminal 3 — Delta
stops.desc: ⏰ 7:30 wake · 8:15 leave the hotel · 8:45 curbside · bags checked and through security by 9:30 · 10:29 boarding. Delta flies out of LAX TERMINAL 3 — confirm on the app the night before, Delta splits between T2 and T3 and gate assignments move. Saturday morning LAX security is the busy one, so 9:30 airside is the number that matters, not the 10:59 departure. No car, so leaving 'a bit later' is not a lever you have. Lands San Antonio 3:59 PM. Trip done — 8 days, one whole coast.
